text:
sam: quick sync — thinking about autoscaler backoff/handoff during dedicated pool migrations. rough idea: central scaler proposes target, operator does node ops but needs backoff window to avoid flip-flops. thoughts?

maria: +1. we saw oscillation on pool-7 last week when predictive burst and reactive fallback overlapped.

alex: can we add hysteresis + time-based decay? require a sustained delta for 60s before scale-down. prevents thrashing.

jia: agree. also operator should be allowed to override for emergency scale-ups (e.g., tenant SLA violations). needs an emergency_priority flag.

sam: proposed config sketch:

```
autoscaler:
  target_headroom: 3
  min_stable_duration: 60s
  scale_down_backoff: 2m
  scale_up_emergency_threshold: 0.9
  emergency_priority: true
```

alex: nit: make backoff exponential for repeated reversals: 2m, 4m, 8m, cap 30m.

maria: rollout plan idea: central computes intent and publishes intent_version; operator applies but will enforce min_stable_duration and backoff on opposing ops. start with 10% tenants for 48h.

deploy-bot: canary applied to cluster-42 (canary-tenant=redwood-test)

alex: also emit telemetry tags: intent_version, operator_applied_version, decision_reason (hysteresis|override|emergency). that'll help debug oscillations.

jia: @sam can you add a simple sim harness in the PR to validate backoff behavior under bursty traces?

sam: on it. I'll open PR and link to this thread. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234

maria: LGTM. After canary, watch: scale_count, oscillation_rate, time_to_stable. set alert if oscillation_rate > 0.03 for 1h.

sam: thanks all — I'll draft the rollout runbook and add tests. keeping this thread for followups.
